name: McMurdo Long Duration Balloon Facility

operator_text.quote: NASA Long Duration Balloon (LDB) site at LDB Camp, McMurdo Station.

intervals.label: used for ANITA balloon launches
intervals.quote: ANITA-LITE launched December 17, 2003 and flew for ~18.5 days onboard a NASA LDB scientific balloon during the 2003 Austral Summer from McMurdo Base, Antarctica
intervals.note: This facility record covers only the NASA LDB launch operations relevant to ANITA; it is not a full model of the wider McMurdo Station complex.

notes: This is the NASA long-duration-balloon launch facility used to fly ANITA, not a detector site: ANITA takes data at float altitude (~37 km) over the Antarctic ice sheet, not at the launch point. Different ANITA flights launched from slightly different pads near McMurdo Station (LDB Camp for ANITA-LITE and ANITA-I; Williams Field for ANITA-II per the collaboration's own campaign pages); both are modelled as one facility here since no source distinguishes them as administratively separate.
Derived fields (site_ids, accelerator_ids, beamline_ids, institution_id, document_ids, experiment_ids) are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).

summary.plain: The NASA balloon-launch site near McMurdo Station, Antarctica, where the ANITA neutrino instrument was launched on each of its long, high-altitude balloon flights.
summary.technical: NASA Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility (CSBF) long-duration-balloon launch operations near McMurdo Station, Antarctica, used to launch ANITA-LITE (2003), ANITA-I (2006), ANITA-II (2008, from Williams Field), ANITA-III (2014) and ANITA-IV (2016).
